decisions.reason: The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY capturing Lit Protocol gating, automatic ownership verification, encrypted delivery, the gated-viewer destination, and the seamless access flow.
Automatic ownership verification changes how book access is gated, not which entitlements or NFT-linked state transfer to a secondary buyer.
The metadata destination and gated book-access flow do not alter secondary-sale royalty enforcement, amount, or type.
Changing the metadata link target to a gated viewer does not change the unlimited-mint NFT ebook collection model.
The source decision does not request or necessarily entail any change to the product FAQ copy.
The gated-viewer and ownership-verification decision does not change prize-ticket counters or dashboard ticket accounting.
The NFT metadata may link to a gated viewer while still displaying and deriving the referral code exactly as currently required.
Lit Protocol supplies access gating and does not necessarily replace the read-only PDF.js viewer, its entry points, or its default viewing mode.
Book-access gating and metadata routing do not affect automatic prize delivery to winners' wallets.
The book was already required to use removable Pinata/IPFS storage; routing metadata through a Lit-gated viewer does not change that storage state.
The source specifically changes the NFT metadata destination and does not necessarily alter the certificate email's contents, labels, or read action.
NFT ownership verification for book access is unrelated to Chainlink VRF winner selection and its verification method.
